newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH METAL, ENGINEERING LOBBY SEES POSITIVE '97.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH METAL, ENGINEERING LOBBY SEES POSITIVE '97.

text.p: The prospects for the Finnish metal industry this year are positive, the branch federation said in its 1996 year-book published on Tuesday.
"Positive market trends are foreseen, both in exports and on the home market, in most of the subsectors," the Federation of Finnish Metal, Engineering and Electrotechnical Industries said.
Rapid growth in Finland and higher growth rates in other EU member states gave a good ground for further favourable development, it said.

"In Finland the most marked change will be the clear turn up of the building construction trend, after many years of decline," it said. This would increase the demand for builders' hardware, the federation said.
But there were as yet no signs of an awaited pick-up of forest industry investments in Europe and North-America.

Profitability of most metal, engineering and electronics industry companies had developed positively in the last few years. "There are no marked pressures towards weakening price competitiveness," it said.
The metal, engineering and electronics industry is the largest industrial branch in Finland, accounting for a good third of the total industrial value-added, the federation said.
Last year, the growth of production of these industries slowed down to six percent from 20 percent in 1995. Growth was fastest last year in the electronics and electrical goods branch.
Exports of metals, engineering and electronics products made up 50 percent of total Finnish goods export in 1996, up from about 48 percent the previous year.
